Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the InnovaTech Solutions Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Jennifer Lee, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Lee, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to InnovaTech Solutions’ third quarter earnings call. Joining me today are Robert Thompson, CEO; Susan Davis, CFO; and Michael Chen, Chief Technology Officer.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and presentation, which are available on our Investor Relations site. Today’s discussion may include forward-looking statements. With that, let me turn the call over to Robert.

Robert Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Jennifer, and welcome everyone.

We’re pleased with our performance this quarter. I want to highlight a few areas.

Let's start with our P&L guidance for the upcoming fourth quarter. We anticipate revenue to land within the range of $12.4 billion to $12.7 billion. At the midpoint of $12.55 billion, this represents a 3.4% sequential increase compared to the $12.14 billion we recorded in Q3. This projected sequential growth is primarily fueled by several key factors. We typically experience a surge in demand for our consumer electronics segment during the holiday season, which historically drives a significant portion of our Q4 revenue. We project this segment will contribute approximately $4.8 billion to the total Q4 revenue, representing a 7% increase compared to Q3's $4.48 billion. This includes strong anticipated sales for our new flagship smartphone model, the 'Apex X', and our updated line of smart home devices. Early pre-order data for the Apex X has been exceptionally strong, exceeding internal projections by 15%, which indicates a healthy consumer appetite despite the current macroeconomic climate. Our cloud services division, 'Nimbus Solutions', continues to be a robust growth engine. We expect Nimbus Solutions to generate around $3.9 billion in revenue during Q4, a 5% increase from the $3.7 billion in Q3. This growth is supported by increased adoption of our AI-powered analytics platform and the onboarding of several new enterprise clients, particularly in the healthcare and financial services sectors. We've seen a particularly strong uptake of our security solutions within Nimbus, driven by heightened cybersecurity concerns across the enterprise landscape. While not as pronounced as the consumer electronics or cloud services segments, we project a modest 1.5% sequential increase in our enterprise software revenue, reaching approximately $2.23 billion in Q4 from $2.2 billion in Q3. This growth is primarily attributed to recurring subscription revenue from our existing customer base and strategic upselling of premium features within our software suite. However, longer sales cycles and increased price sensitivity in the current economic environment are tempering overall growth in this segment. North America is expected to remain our largest market, contributing approximately 45% of total Q4 revenue. We project a 3% sequential increase in North America. Europe is expected to see a similar growth rate of around 3.5%, driven by increased demand for our cloud services. Asia-Pacific, excluding China, is projected to experience slightly higher growth of 4%, fueled by strong performance in India and Southeast Asia. However, we anticipate a more muted performance in China due to ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and increased competition from domestic players. We are implementing targeted marketing campaigns and strategic partnerships in these key growth regions to further penetrate the market. Turning to gross margin, we are guiding for a range of 51.5% to 53.5% for Q4. This range reflects a balanced outlook considering both positive and negative factors influencing our cost structure. We anticipate benefiting from improved component pricing for our consumer electronics products, particularly for memory chips and display panels. We secured favorable long-term contracts with key suppliers earlier in the year, which will positively impact our cost of goods sold in Q4. Furthermore, the increasing contribution of our higher-margin cloud services business is expected to positively impact our overall gross margin. Our Nimbus solutions have a significantly higher gross margin (estimated around 70%) than our hardware segments. The strong US dollar could have an adverse impact on revenue. We have hedged some of our currency exposure, but this will not offset all of the impact. Additionally, we continue to invest heavily in research and development (R&D), particularly in the areas of AI, machine learning, and next-generation hardware technologies, which will impact our operating expenses. While these investments are crucial for our long-term growth and competitive advantage, they will also impact our short-term profitability. The mix of products sold in Q4 will also influence our gross margin. The higher proportion of consumer electronics sales, which generally have lower gross margins compared to cloud services, will have a slightly dilutive effect. However, this is partially offset by the anticipated strong performance of the Apex X, which boasts a premium price point and a healthy gross margin. Finally, we are guiding for an operating margin between 40.5% and 42.5%. This reflects our continued commitment to operational efficiency and cost management. We are actively streamlining our operations, automating key processes, and leveraging data analytics to optimize resource allocation. However, as mentioned earlier, our ongoing investments in R&D and strategic marketing initiatives will continue to impact our operating expenses. Looking ahead, we are focused on several key strategic initiatives to drive sustainable revenue growth and improve profitability. These include expanding our cloud services portfolio by actively developing new cloud-based solutions for various industries, including healthcare, finance, and manufacturing. We believe that AI will be a key differentiator in the future, and we are investing heavily in AI research and development across all of our business segments. We are working to diversify our supply chain and improve our resilience to disruptions. And we are committed to providing our customers with the best possible products and services. In conclusion, while we acknowledge the ongoing macroeconomic uncertainties, we are confident in our ability to deliver solid results in Q4. Our strong product portfolio, diversified revenue streams, and disciplined approach to cost management position us well to navigate the current environment and achieve our long-term growth objectives. We believe the guidance reflects a balanced view of the opportunities and challenges ahead, and we remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering value to our shareholders.

Next, I want to address our wafer sales performance. Our Q3 2024 wafer sales demonstrate a continued shift towards advanced process technologies, solidifying our position as a leading foundry for high-performance computing, mobile, and AI applications. We achieved a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year, reaching $2.3 billion, driven primarily by demand for our advanced nodes. Gross margin landed at a healthy 48%, reflecting optimized operational efficiencies and a favorable product mix. Advanced technologies (defined as 16nm and below) collectively accounted for a substantial 61% of total wafer revenue this quarter. This underscores the increasing complexity and performance demands across various end markets. The revenue generated from advanced nodes totaled $1.403 billion. The 5nm process node is quickly becoming a major contributor. It accounted for 8% of wafer revenue in Q3, translating to approximately $184 million. The average selling price (ASP) for 5nm wafers remained premium, averaging around $18,000 per wafer. While unit volume is still relatively low compared to more mature nodes, the rapid adoption in high-end smartphone SoCs and initial AI accelerator applications resulted in a 25% sequential increase in 5nm wafer shipments. We are actively working with several fabless clients to optimize their 5nm designs, leading to increased yields and further cost efficiencies. We project 5nm to exceed 15% of total wafer revenue by Q1 2025. We anticipate a slight ASP decrease in Q4 as production matures and we onboard more volume-sensitive clients. However, the volume increase will offset this, maintaining healthy revenue contribution. A significant amount of the 5nm product is coming from our Arizona facility. 7nm continues to be a major revenue driver, representing 35% of wafer sales, or approximately $805 million. Its strong performance is fueled by a diverse range of applications, including data center CPUs/GPUs, gaming consoles, and automotive processors. The ASP for 7nm wafers averaged around $12,000, reflecting the balance between performance and cost-effectiveness. We observed a 10% increase in 7nm wafer shipments compared to Q2, primarily due to increased demand from our key North American customer for its data center GPU. The 7nm node, despite its age, is still very important in revenue generation. 16nm contributed 18% to wafer revenue, representing approximately $414 million. This node benefits from its established infrastructure and optimized manufacturing processes, leading to high yields and competitive pricing. The ASP for 16nm wafers averaged around $7,000. While growth is relatively flat, 16nm provides stable revenue and cash flow, particularly in applications such as IoT devices, display drivers, and certain automotive components. Our partnership with a major European automotive manufacturer continues to drive strong 16nm volume. Nodes above 16nm accounted for the remaining 39% of wafer revenue ($897 million). While these nodes are experiencing a gradual decline in overall contribution, they remain strategically important for supporting a wide range of applications, including power management ICs, analog components, and embedded memory. We are actively managing capacity allocation for these nodes, optimizing utilization rates, and selectively raising prices in areas where demand remains strong and capacity is constrained. We are also exploring partnerships to potentially divest certain legacy fab capacity to focus on advanced node expansion. North America remains our largest market, driven by demand for 7nm and 5nm wafers for data center and AI applications. We're seeing increasing interest in domestic manufacturing, which bodes well for our US-based facilities. Asia-Pacific demand is strong across all nodes, particularly in the mobile and consumer electronics segments. We are closely monitoring geopolitical risks in the region and diversifying our supply chain to mitigate potential disruptions. The automotive sector is a key driver of demand in Europe, particularly for 16nm and mature nodes. We are actively engaging with European OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers to secure long-term partnerships. We are heavily investing in the development of next-generation process technologies, including 3nm and beyond. Our R&D spending increased by 12% year-over-year, reflecting our commitment to maintaining technological leadership. We are expanding our production capacity for 5nm and 7nm wafers to meet growing demand. New fab construction is underway in Taiwan and the US, with expected completion dates in 2025 and 2026, respectively. We are implementing advanced process control (APC) and yield management systems to optimize manufacturing efficiency and improve wafer quality. Our strategy is to remain at the forefront of advanced process technology, enabling our customers to develop innovative products and capture market share. We are focused on diversifying our customer base and expanding our presence in emerging markets, such as AI, automotive, and IoT. We are committed to sustainable manufacturing practices and are investing in renewable energy and water conservation initiatives. In conclusion, Q3 2024 was another strong quarter for wafer sales, driven by the increasing demand for advanced process technologies. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver sustainable growth and profitability. We expect the trend of advanced node adoption to continue, fueled by the increasing complexity and performance demands of modern computing applications. The management team is confident that our investments in R&D and capacity expansion will ensure our continued leadership in the foundry market.

Finally, let's address net margin and diluted EPS performance. Our Q3 diluted EPS reached NT$5.3, and Return on Equity (ROE) landed at a strong 31.3%. The NT$5.3 diluted EPS represents a significant 12% increase compared to the NT$4.75 reported in Q3 of the previous fiscal year. This growth is primarily attributable to a confluence of factors: a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion (USD), improvements in operational efficiency, and a favorable tax rate. However, it's crucial to understand the nuances behind this EPS figure. Specifically, a one-time gain of $25 million (USD) from the sale of a non-core asset in our European operations contributed approximately NT$0.3 to the EPS. While this is a positive development, it’s essential to recognize that it's not indicative of core operational performance. Excluding this one-time gain, the underlying EPS growth would be closer to 6.5%, still a healthy rate, but one that needs to be viewed in the context of our ongoing investments. Furthermore, the diluted EPS calculation factors in the potential dilution from outstanding stock options and restricted stock units. We saw a slight increase in the weighted average number of shares outstanding, from 420 million to 425 million, due to the exercise of some employee stock options. This dilution slightly dampened the overall EPS growth. Our Q3 net margin saw an improvement of approximately 180 basis points (1.8%) compared to Q3 of last year. This improvement is primarily driven by supply chain optimization. Our ongoing investments in supply chain digitalization and diversification are yielding tangible results. We successfully negotiated better pricing with key suppliers, particularly in the semiconductor and raw materials sectors, leading to a reduction in the cost of goods sold (COGS) as a percentage of revenue by approximately 100 basis points. The implementation of lean manufacturing principles across our production facilities has resulted in significant efficiency gains, reducing waste and improving throughput. This has translated into lower operating expenses as a percentage of revenue. We also saw benefits from the rollout of our AI-powered predictive maintenance system, minimizing downtime and improving equipment utilization. And we are strategically shifting our product mix towards higher-margin offerings, particularly in the enterprise solutions and premium consumer segments. This shift has contributed positively to the overall net margin. In Q3, revenue from our enterprise solutions segment grew by 22%, significantly outpacing the growth of our more commoditized consumer products. However, we are also facing some headwinds that are impacting our net margin, including increased marketing and sales expenses. We have strategically increased our marketing and sales investments to support the launch of our new flagship product line and to expand our market share in key regions, particularly in Southeast Asia. These investments, while necessary for long-term growth, have put pressure on our operating expenses. The strengthening of the US dollar against several major currencies, including the Euro and the Japanese Yen, has negatively impacted our reported net margin. While we have hedging strategies in place, they only partially mitigate the impact of these fluctuations. And we are experiencing inflationary pressures across various cost categories, including labor, energy, and transportation. While we are actively managing these costs, they are still impacting our profitability. Our North American and European operations showed strong revenue growth and improved profitability, driven by strong demand for our enterprise solutions and premium consumer products. However, our Asia-Pacific region, excluding China, experienced slower growth due to increased competition and macroeconomic headwinds. We are investing heavily in digital transformation across all aspects of our business, from supply chain management to customer engagement. This is enabling us to improve efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance customer experience. Our recent launch of the QuantumLeap line has been well-received by the market and is contributing to our revenue growth and profitability. We are strategically expanding our presence in key growth markets, particularly in Southeast Asia and Latin America. This will enable us to diversify our revenue streams and reduce our reliance on mature markets. While our Q3 performance was strong, we are facing some challenges in the near term, including increased competition, macroeconomic uncertainty, and inflationary pressures. We remain confident in our ability to navigate these challenges and deliver sustainable, long-term growth. We will continue to focus on driving operational efficiency, investing in innovation, and expanding our presence in key growth markets. In summary, the third quarter results, anchored by the NT$5.3 EPS and 31.3% ROE, showcase a company executing on its strategic vision. While the headline numbers are positive and showcase improvement, understanding the nuanced drivers – the one-time gains, the impact of dilution, the improvements in supply chain, and the headwinds from currency and inflation – is critical for a complete picture. Our continued investment in digital transformation, new product development, and geographic expansion will be vital to maintaining this momentum and delivering long-term value to our shareholders. We anticipate continued, albeit potentially moderated, growth in the coming quarters as we navigate the evolving global landscape.

I’ll now pass it over to Susan to walk through the numbers in more detail.

Susan Davis, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Robert, and hello, everyone.

Let me break it down starting with gross margin results. Our gross margin for Q3 2024 reached 53.4%, representing a 0.4 percentage point increase sequentially from the 53.0% reported in Q2 2024. This positive movement reflects a combination of factors, primarily a significant surge in capacity utilization across our global manufacturing network. Specifically, we saw utilization rates climb to an average of 92% across our key fabs, up from 87% in the previous quarter. This increase was particularly pronounced in our advanced node facilities, driven by robust demand for our high-performance computing (HPC) and automotive solutions. This higher utilization directly translated to improved absorption of fixed manufacturing costs, contributing approximately 0.7 percentage points to the gross margin improvement. We estimate the dollar impact of this utilization increase to be around $45 million in the quarter. However, this positive impact was partially offset by two primary headwinds: the ongoing ramp-up of our 5-nanometer (5nm) production and unfavorable foreign exchange rates. The 5nm ramp, while strategically critical for future growth, carries inherent margin dilution during the initial phases. As we invest in yield optimization and work through the learning curve on this advanced node, we saw a negative impact of approximately 0.2 percentage points on our gross margin, equating to roughly $13 million. This is expected and factored into our guidance, as the initial production runs typically have lower yields and higher costs per wafer. The strengthening of the US dollar against key currencies, particularly the Euro and the Japanese Yen, also negatively impacted our gross margin. We estimate the unfavorable exchange rate impact to be approximately 0.1 percentage points, or about $7 million. We employ hedging strategies to mitigate some of this risk, but these strategies only provide partial protection against significant currency fluctuations. Importantly, our Q3 gross margin of 53.4% exceeded the high end of our previously issued guidance range of 52.5% to 53.0%. The primary driver for this outperformance was the higher-than-anticipated overall capacity utilization rate. We initially projected a utilization rate of approximately 89%, but the strong demand environment, particularly from our key customers in the AI and cloud computing sectors, allowed us to operate our fabs at a higher level of efficiency. This resulted in a roughly $25 million positive variance compared to our initial gross margin projections. Furthermore, while the 5nm ramp impacted margins as anticipated, we saw slightly better-than-expected yield improvements in the latter half of the quarter, contributing modestly to the outperformance. We attribute this to the accelerated learning curve achieved through close collaboration with our equipment suppliers and our internal process optimization efforts. From a regional perspective, North America and Asia (ex-China) showed the strongest demand, leading to a higher utilization of facilities in these regions. While demand in Europe was slightly softer, our targeted cost-optimization initiatives, especially around energy consumption in our European fabs, helped partially mitigate the impact. We are also focusing on strategic pricing adjustments, particularly in regions with stronger demand, to maximize profitability. Our investment in advanced packaging technologies is proving beneficial. The increased adoption of our 2.5D and 3D packaging solutions has allowed us to capture higher value per wafer, positively impacting gross margin. We are aggressively pursuing yield enhancement programs across all technology nodes. These initiatives include advanced statistical process control, predictive maintenance, and data-driven process optimization. We are committed to reducing our energy consumption and carbon footprint. Our investments in renewable energy sources and energy-efficient equipment are not only environmentally responsible but also contribute to lowering our operating costs and improving gross margins. Looking ahead to the fourth quarter of 2024, we anticipate a slight decline in gross margin. We currently project a gross margin of 52.5% at the midpoint of our guidance range, representing a 0.9 percentage point sequential decrease from the 53.4% achieved in Q3. This projected decline is primarily attributable to two key factors: the continued, steep ramp-up of our 5nm production and the expectation of a less favorable foreign exchange rate environment. The 5nm ramp is expected to accelerate significantly in Q4, with a substantial increase in wafer starts dedicated to this advanced node. While this volume growth is crucial for meeting customer demand and driving future revenue, the initial stages of the ramp will continue to exert downward pressure on our gross margin. We anticipate the 5nm ramp to dilute gross margin by approximately 0.6 percentage points in Q4, equating to an estimated $40 million impact. Furthermore, based on current market conditions and forward currency curves, we expect the foreign exchange rate environment to become less favorable in Q4. We are factoring in a negative impact of approximately 0.3 percentage points, or about $20 million, related to currency fluctuations. While we are actively pursuing cost optimization initiatives and yield improvement programs to mitigate these headwinds, the magnitude of the 5nm ramp and the projected currency impact will likely outweigh these efforts in the near term. In summary, our Q3 gross margin performance was strong, driven by robust demand and high capacity utilization. Looking ahead to Q4, we anticipate a slight decline due to the accelerating 5nm ramp and unfavorable foreign exchange rates. We remain focused on executing our strategic initiatives, optimizing our cost structure, and driving long-term gross margin improvement. We are confident in our ability to navigate these challenges and deliver sustainable value to our shareholders.

Now, moving to wafer sales. As Robert mentioned, our Q3 2024 wafer sales demonstrate a continued shift towards advanced process technologies. Advanced technologies (defined as 16nm and below) collectively accounted for a substantial 61% of total wafer revenue this quarter. This underscores the increasing complexity and performance demands across various end markets. The 5nm process node is quickly becoming a major contributor. It accounted for 8% of wafer revenue in Q3, translating to approximately $184 million. 7nm continues to be a major revenue driver, representing 35% of wafer sales, or approximately $805 million. 16nm contributed 18% to wafer revenue, representing approximately $414 million. Nodes above 16nm accounted for the remaining 39% of wafer revenue ($897 million). While these nodes are experiencing a gradual decline in overall contribution, they remain strategically important for supporting a wide range of applications.

Lastly, I'd like to briefly touch on comments on inventory or DOI for this quarter. Our DOI increased by three days, reaching 58 days at the close of Q3. The primary contributor to the DOI increase is the ongoing ramp-up of our N5 production capacity. As you know, N5 is a critical node for several key applications, including high-performance computing (HPC), AI accelerators, and now, increasingly, advanced smartphone processors. To support the anticipated demand, and as previously communicated in Q2's earnings call, we strategically increased our N5 wafer starts by approximately 25% compared to Q2. This naturally translates to a higher level of work-in-progress (WIP) and finished goods inventory related to N5. Specifically, N5-related inventory accounted for roughly 45% of the overall inventory increase this quarter. We anticipate N5 inventory levels to stabilize by Q4 as production efficiencies improve and product is shipped to customers. Looking downstream, we observed that our fabless customers' overall inventory levels, while still elevated, are showing signs of stabilization. They exited Q3 with inventory levels approximately 12% above historical seasonal averages. This is down slightly from the 15% increase we saw last quarter. This strategic inventory build is a direct response to the ongoing geopolitical uncertainties and the continued emphasis on supply chain security. Our customers, particularly those serving the high-growth 5G smartphone market, are proactively mitigating potential disruptions by carrying higher safety stocks. We've seen a particularly pronounced build-up in inventory related to advanced packaging solutions, specifically in the fan-out wafer-level packaging (FOWLP) segment. This is driven by the increasing complexity of 5G smartphone SoCs and the need for robust interconnect solutions. Some of our key customers, such as Apex Devices and Quantum Solutions, have explicitly communicated their intention to maintain higher-than-normal inventory levels of these components for at least the next two quarters. We are working closely with them to ensure we can meet their demands while managing our own inventory efficiently. In China, we've observed a more aggressive inventory build-up among some of our domestic customers, driven by both supply chain security concerns and anticipation of increased demand related to government initiatives aimed at bolstering domestic semiconductor capabilities. We estimate that approximately 30% of the fabless customer inventory increase is attributable to Chinese customers. We are closely monitoring this situation to ensure compliance with all relevant export regulations and to proactively manage any potential risks associated with inventory obsolescence. We are actively implementing several initiatives to optimize inventory management and mitigate the impact of the elevated DOI. We've invested in advanced AI-powered demand forecasting tools that leverage real-time market data and customer order patterns to improve the accuracy of our production planning. We are seeing early signs of success, with a 5% reduction in forecast error rates for key product lines. We are working closely with our suppliers to improve lead times and increase the flexibility of our supply chain. This includes exploring dual-sourcing options for critical materials and components. We are implementing a more granular inventory segmentation strategy, categorizing inventory based on factors such as demand volatility, lead times, and obsolescence risk. This allows us to tailor our inventory management policies to the specific characteristics of each product line. We expect this initiative to reduce excess and obsolete inventory by at least 8% within the next two quarters. We are adjusting our production schedules to better align with customer demand and reduce WIP inventory. This includes implementing more frequent production runs and shorter cycle times. And we are strengthening our collaborative planning processes with key customers to improve demand visibility and reduce the risk of inventory imbalances. This involves sharing real-time data on demand forecasts, production schedules, and inventory levels. While we expect inventory levels to remain above historical seasonal levels for the next couple of quarters due to the ongoing emphasis on supply chain security, we are confident that the strategic initiatives we are implementing will enable us to optimize inventory management and mitigate any potential negative impacts on our financial performance. We project DOI to plateau around 56-59 days in Q4 and start to normalize in the second half of next year. Our overall strategy remains focused on ensuring supply chain security while proactively managing inventory levels to optimize working capital and maximize shareholder value. We will continue to closely monitor the situation and provide updates as necessary.

Now, let me hand things over to Michael to talk about product and operational progress.

Michael Chen, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Susan.

This was a busy quarter for our teams. On the innovation front, we made meaningful advances around sales by segment and platforms. We achieved a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year, landing at $2.3 billion. Our smartphone platform continues to be a cornerstone of our business. We saw a robust 12% quarter-over-quarter increase in revenue within this segment, reaching $1.058 billion. This growth was driven by several factors. Firstly, the successful launch of our new "Apex" series processors, featuring our proprietary "NeuralBoost" AI engine, has been exceptionally well-received by leading smartphone manufacturers. We are seeing increased demand for these chips, particularly in the high-end and flagship device categories. Geographically, we witnessed particularly strong uptake in the Asia-Pacific region, specifically in India and Southeast Asia, where demand for advanced mobile processing power is accelerating. Our average selling price (ASP) within the smartphone segment increased by approximately 5% quarter-over-quarter, reflecting the shift towards higher-value, feature-rich chips. Gross margins in the smartphone segment remain healthy at 52%. While increased competition from domestic Chinese manufacturers is a factor we are constantly monitoring, our technological lead in AI processing and power efficiency has allowed us to maintain a premium pricing position and defend our margins. HPC was a significant growth driver this quarter. We experienced a substantial 25% quarter-over-quarter increase, contributing $851 million to our total revenue. This surge is primarily attributed to the escalating demand for our "QuantumLeap" series of GPUs, particularly in the areas of artificial intelligence training, machine learning inference, and scientific simulations. We secured several major contracts with leading cloud service providers and research institutions during the quarter, further solidifying our position as a key enabler of the AI revolution. A key design win with a major US-based supercomputing center also contributed significantly. The HPC segment boasts our highest gross margins, currently at 65%. This reflects the high value and specialized nature of our HPC solutions, as well as the significant R&D investment we have made in this area. We anticipate continued strong demand for our HPC offerings in the coming quarters, driven by the insatiable need for compute power to support AI development and other computationally intensive workloads. The IoT segment continues its steady expansion, with a 24% quarter-over-quarter increase, generating $207 million in revenue. Growth is broad-based across various IoT applications, including industrial automation, smart home devices, and connected healthcare. Our "ConnectCore" series of low-power, high-performance processors is gaining traction in the market, enabling a wide range of IoT devices with enhanced connectivity and processing capabilities. We are actively investing in expanding our IoT ecosystem through strategic partnerships with software vendors and device manufacturers. We are also seeing initial success with our new "EdgeAI" chips, which bring AI processing directly to the edge of the network, reducing latency and improving security. Gross margins in the IoT segment are currently at 48%. We are actively working to improve margins through cost optimization initiatives and a focus on higher-value, integrated solutions. The automotive sector presented challenges this quarter, experiencing a 23% quarter-over-quarter decline to $46 million. This decline is primarily due to ongoing supply chain constraints affecting the automotive industry, as well as a delay in the ramp-up of a key automotive project related to autonomous driving. While the short-term outlook remains uncertain, we remain confident in the long-term potential of the automotive market. We are actively working with our automotive partners to address the supply chain issues and accelerate the deployment of our automotive solutions. We expect new contracts to come into effect in Q1 2024 that will improve the situation. Automotive margins are currently at 40%, impacted by lower volumes and increased component costs. We are taking steps to mitigate these challenges and improve profitability in this segment. The digital consumer electronics segment experienced a 24% quarter-over-quarter decrease, contributing $69 million to our total revenue. This decline reflects the overall slowdown in the consumer electronics market, as well as increased competition from lower-cost alternatives. We are actively repositioning our DCE offerings to focus on higher-value applications, such as premium audio and video processing, where we can leverage our technological strengths. DCE margins are currently at 42%, reflecting the competitive pricing environment. We are focused on streamlining our product portfolio and reducing costs to improve profitability in this segment. Overall, we are pleased with our Q3 performance, particularly the strong growth in our smartphone and HPC platforms. While the automotive and DCE segments faced headwinds, we are confident in our ability to navigate these challenges and capitalize on the long-term growth opportunities in these markets. Our strategic focus on innovation, particularly in AI and high-performance computing, is driving our success and positioning us for continued growth in the years to come. We continue to invest heavily in R&D, allocating 25% of revenue to these activities. This investment is critical for maintaining our technological leadership and developing innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers. We are also actively pursuing strategic acquisitions and partnerships to expand our capabilities and accelerate our growth. Looking ahead to Q4, we anticipate continued strong demand for our smartphone and HPC solutions, and we expect to see a gradual recovery in the automotive and DCE segments. We are confident in our ability to deliver solid financial results in the fourth quarter and beyond.

Let’s now open the floor for questions.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks for taking my question. On the sales by segment, could you expand on what’s driving that strength in HPC, particularly compared to the softness in automotive?

Robert Thompson:
Certainly. The HPC strength is really a story of AI. The demand for our QuantumLeap GPUs for AI training is just insatiable. We are seeing cloud providers and research institutions alike scrambling for compute power, and our solutions are at the leading edge. As for automotive, as we mentioned, the supply chain issues are still a factor, but more importantly, a key autonomous driving project experienced a delay. We expect that to ramp up again in Q1.

Analyst 2:
A follow-up on the comments on inventory. How confident are you that you can manage that N5 inventory build-up, given the uncertainties in the global economy?

Susan Davis:
We’re very confident. We've stress-tested our demand forecasts extensively, and we have strong visibility into our customers' needs. The N5 node is critical for several key applications, and we believe the demand is sustainable. Also, the inventory segmentation and management strategies we’ve put in place will help us to quickly adapt to any changes in the market.

Analyst 3:
And for the sales by segment, any update on the autonomous driving ramp-up in the automotive sector?

Michael Chen:
Yes, we are working closely with our automotive partners to resolve the issues that caused the delay. We expect the project to resume its ramp-up in Q1 2024. We are also exploring new partnerships to expand our presence in the automotive market. The long-term prospects for our automotive solutions remain very strong.

Analyst 4:
Just a final one — on the gross margin, is the outperformance mostly due to the higher utilization, or are there other factors at play?

Susan Davis:
The higher utilization was the primary driver, but we also saw slightly better-than-expected yield improvements on the 5nm node towards the end of the quarter. Our energy efficiency initiatives are also contributing to lower operating costs.

Closing

Robert Thompson:
Thank you again for joining us today. We remain confident in our long-term growth story and are committed to disciplined execution. We appreciate your continued interest and support.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.

HPC experienced a substantial 25% QoQ increase, contributing $851 million with a gross margin of 65%. IoT segment increased 24% QoQ, generating $207 million with a gross margin of 48%. Automotive declined 23% QoQ to $46 million with a gross margin of 40%. Digital Consumer Electronics (DCE) decreased 24% QoQ to $69 million with a gross margin of 42%.
aspect_summary.Net margin and Diluted EPS (earnings per: Q3 diluted EPS was NT$5.3, a 12% increase YoY. This includes a one-time gain of $25 million (USD) which contributed approximately NT$0.3 to the EPS. The underlying EPS growth excluding this gain would be closer to 6.5%. Q3 net margin improved by approximately 180 basis points (1.8%) compared to Q3 of last year.
aspect_summary.wafer sales and the breakdown to wafer q: Q3 wafer sales increased 15% YoY, reaching $2.3 billion. Advanced technologies (16nm and below) accounted for 61% of total wafer revenue. 5nm accounted for 8% of wafer revenue ($184 million) with an ASP of $18,000 per wafer. 7nm represented 35% of wafer sales ($805 million) with an ASP of $12,000. 16nm contributed 18% ($414 million) with an ASP of $7,000. Nodes above 16nm accounted for the remaining 39% ($897 million).
aspect_summary.Gross margin results, QoQ changes, YoY c: Q3 gross margin was 53.4%, a 0.4 percentage point increase sequentially from Q2 2024. This was driven by higher capacity utilization. The 5nm ramp and unfavorable foreign exchange rates partially offset the increase. It exceeded the previously issued guidance range of 52.5% to 53.0% due to higher-than-anticipated overall capacity utilization rate.
